data.title: CapitaLand Ascendas REIT posts 9.9% rental reversion in Q3
data.description:
Portfolio occupancy remained healthy at 90.1%.

CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (Clar) posted a 9.9% rental reversion in the third quarter (Q3), bringing its nine-month (9M) average to 9%, with momentum expected to hold for the rest of the year.

Overall occupancy inched up slightly to 90.1% quarter on quarter (QoQ), up from June’s 89.1% rate.

The firm’s portfolio amounts to $20.7b as of 30 September, with Singapore accounting for 66% at $13.8b.

Clar said that it is steering its portfolio to cater to changing market and tenant demands, focusing on Business Space and Life Sciences ($8.8b), Logistics ($5.5b) and Industrial and Data Centres ($6.4b).

Q3 average debt stood at 3.4%, with aggregate leverage of 41.8%, driven by higher borrowings to fund acquisitions, Clar said.

In Singapore, the firm completed the acquisition of two logistics properties, 5 Tus Avenue 5 ($133.9m) and 25 Loyang Crescent ($504.2m), for $638.1m. They are expected to yield 6.6% and 6.9%, respectively.

Clar is also divesting three properties in Singapore totalling a sale price of $281.7m, namely Kim Chuan Telecommunications Complex ($200.4m), 17 Changi Business Park Central 1 ($60m), and 9 Serangoon North Avenue 5 ($21.3m).

The properties are estimated to be sold at $255m. If fully used to repay debts, the proceeds are expected to reduce aggregate leverage to 41%.

The occupancy rate in Singapore inched up to 90.9% in September 2026, up from 90.1% in June 2026, driven by fully occupied new acquisitions and higher occupancy in the logistics portfolio.

Meanwhile, rental reversions in Singapore decreased from 5% to 4.3% QoQ.

Clar leads in green energy amongst S-REITs in Singapore, with an additional 12 properties with solar panels this year, totalling 42 properties with solar generation.

data.title: Mi Material revenue jumps 15.6% on chip packaging demand
data.description:
Revenue surged to $117m from $83.4m YoY.

Mi Material Holding Limited reported a gross profit of $54m (US$42.6m) in the first nine months (9M), driven by sustained demand for its solder spheres in semiconductor packaging.

The group recently debuted on the Singapore Exchange (SGX) Mainboard through a $215m semiconductor offering.

Gross profit margin for the third quarter (Q3) stood at 47.6%, broadly stable from 48% in the second quarter (Q2). For 9M2026, gross profit margin improved to 46.6%, from 45.8% in the first half of the year.

The group attributed the improvement to a shift towards higher-margin proprietary alloys, alongside higher sales volumes and selling prices. Its adjusted profit after tax margin also rose to 28.1% in 9M2026, from 26.6% in the first half.

Revenue reached US$37.8m in Q3, up 15.6% from US$32.7m in Q2, driven primarily by higher sales volumes and sustained customer demand for its patented alloy solder spheres.

Mi Material said demand across the high-performance computing (HPC), memory, mobility and wearables segments is expected to support its performance for the remainder of the financial year.

The group expects positive revenue momentum to continue in the fourth quarter, traditionally its strongest quarter, supported by demand for advanced semiconductor packaging materials.

“As we enter what is traditionally our strongest quarter, we are optimistic about the opportunities ahead,” said Kevin Tan, CEO of Mi Material.

He said the group is well-positioned to expand manufacturing capacity, advance research and development initiatives, and create long-term value for shareholders.

data.title: Starhill Global REIT NPI up 2.3% YoY in Q1
data.description:
Gross revenue rose 1.2% to $48.9m, whilst committed occupancy stood at 97.4%

Starhill Global REIT reported a net property income (NPI) of $38.8m in the first quarter of fiscal year (FY) 2026/27, up 2.3% year-on-year (YoY) from $37.9m.

Gross revenue also increased 1.2% to $48.9m, from $48.3m in the same period last FY.

The gains were mainly attributed to higher contributions from the office components of Ngee Ann City and Myer Centre Adelaide and a lower rental arrears provision, mainly for China Property in Chengdu, 

It was also driven by the appreciation of the Australian dollar and Malaysian ringgit against the Singapore dollar.

They were partially offset by the loss of contributions from divested Wisma Atria Office strata units and lower contributions from Wisma Atria Property's retail component due to tenant transitional downtime.

The NPI would have increased 3.3% YoY excluding the effects of divestment.

Portfolio occupancy stood at 97.4% as at the end of September, with a weighted average lease expiry of 7.1 years by gross rental income.

Gearing stood at 36%, with an average interest rate of 3.7% a year and 80% of debt on fixed or hedged rate.

Meanwhile, Starhill Global REIT announced it will be divesting Ebisu Fort in Tokyo for about $50.2m, a 53.8% premium to its latest independent valuation.

The sale of the freehold, seven-storey retail and office building will mark the the REIT's exit from the Japan market.

data.title: DayOne and Sembcorp unit to evaluate on-site power for data centres
data.description:
The partnership also covers renewable energy supply and maintenance services.

DayOne Data Centers and Sembcorp Utilities have inked a partnership to explore the integration of power and energy solutions into DayOne's data centre developments.

Under a memorandum of understanding, the two will evaluate solutions across areas, including on-site power infrastructure and generation, renewable energy supply, and operations and maintenance services.

DayOne and Sembcorp intend to jointly evaluate the feasibility, business case, and potential implementation pathways for energy solutions associated with agreed projects.

The collaboration is expected to support DayOne’s continued expansion across Asia, the groups said.

It builds on DayOne’s Bring Your Own Power initiative, which integrates power planning into the early stages of data centre development to identify and secure suitable energy solutions.

The approach aims to reduce execution risks, address increasingly constrained power markets, and provide customers with greater certainty as they scale.

data.title: Sheng Siong net profit up 1.8% YoY in Q3
data.description:
Revenue rose 6.2% to $441.5m as the supermarket chain opened three new stores.

Sheng Siong posted a net profit of $44.6m in the third quarter of 2026, up 1.8% year on year (YoY) from $43.8m.

Revenue increased 6.2% to $441.5m from $415.5m, primarily due to new store openings.

Sheng Siong opened three stores in Q3, bringing the total number opened in the first nine months of the year to seven. Total stores in Singapore stand at 92, up from 84 in the same period last year.

Gross profit also increased 8.6% YoY to $142.3, whilst the gross profit margin improved by 0.7 percentage points to 32.2% as improvements in the sales mix helped offset higher operating costs.

Other income for Q3 went up 5.6% to $6.2m, mainly attributable to higher miscellaneous income from a one-off recognition of rebates received from suppliers.

For the first nine months of 2026, net profit rose 8.1% to $125.5m, whilst revenue increased 9.9% to nearly $1.3b.

Sheng Siong said the Johor Bahru–Singapore Rapid Transit System Link, which is expected to begin passenger service in February 2027, may encourage more cross-border shopping and intensify price competition, although it noted that the actual impact remains uncertain.

Wage increases under the Progressive Wage Model and higher transport costs due to higher diesel prices will continue to keep operating costs elevated, it added.

Looking ahead, the supermarket chain said it will prioritise expansion, underpinned by its new Sungei Kadut distribution centre, which will support more than 120 supermarkets.

data.title: NCS mission centre to move clients past AI pilots
data.description:
It plans to expand its AI engineer team to more than 300 in two years.

NCS has launched its artificial intelligence (AI) mission centre, designed to help public and private organisations move from AI experimentation to full-scale enterprise deployment.

The company said it aims to expand its current team of 100 intelligentisation forward-deployed engineers, who are domain experts in AI and vendor-agnostic, to more than 300 within the next two years.

This will include reskilled internal talent and new hires.

The centre leverages NCS’ Sunshine.AI suite, including Sunshine.core for building and governing enterprise AI agents, and Sunshine.commanderAI for coordinating robots across manufacturers.

It will help clients define priority problems, redesign workflows, test and deploy AI solutions securely in live operations, and turn successful deployments into reusable products.

NCS has also formalised a partnership with Changi Airport Group, the Institute of Mental Health, and Life3 Biotech to jointly develop and scale innovative AI-driven solutions.

data.title: Retrenchments rise to 4,800 in Q3
data.description:
Business reorganisation remained the main driver of layoffs.

Singapore's retrenchments rose to 4,800 in the third quarter (Q3), up from 4,620 in the previous quarter, according to preliminary data from the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

MOM said business reorganisation continued to be the main driver of job cuts, which remained elevated in selected outward-oriented sectors.

The proportion of firms expecting to retrench workers over the next three months also increased to 3.1% in September, from 2.8% in August.

The services sector recorded the highest number of layoffs at 4,000, followed by manufacturing with 700 and construction with 100.

Despite the increase, the incidence of retrenchment remained unchanged at 2.0 per 1,000 employees.

Meanwhile, total employment grew by 27,700 in Q3, more than double the 11,400 recorded in the previous quarter. Non-resident workers accounted for the majority of employment growth, particularly in construction and manufacturing.

The overall unemployment rate remained unchanged at 2% in September, whilst resident and citizen unemployment rates edged up to 3% and 3.1%, respectively.

The proportion of firms expecting to hire over the next three months increased to 42.3% in September, from 30.5% in August.

Firms expecting to raise wages also increased to 19.9%, from 16.9% over the same period, although both hiring and wage expectations remained below July levels.

MOM will release its full Q3 labour market report in mid-December.

data.title: Sentosa and TADA to deploy on-demand AVs from 2027
data.description:
Rides are complimentary during the pilot, operating from 1 p.m. to 7 p.m.

Sentosa Development Corporation (SDC) partners with TADA Mobility (Singapore) Pte Ltd to roll out a pilot of an on-demand shared autonomous vehicle (AV) service on Sentosa by early 2027.

This is the island’s first on-demand shared service to operate across a wide network of locations, complementing Sentosa’s existing roadmap with 27 pick-up and drop-off (PUDO) points, to be launched progressively.

The pilot will explore how the service can reduce waiting times, providing improved ride certainty and shortening connections between transport nodes, hotels and attractions.

The AVs are developed by WeRide, with each vehicle seating up to eight guests, with a safety operator on board.

SDC said the AVs will primarily utilise service roads along Siloso Beach and Palawan Beach, as well as the island’s public roads, so guests can visit beachfront attractions and restaurants without shifting to a beach shuttle.

“This partnership with TADA is also part of our Smart Sentosa ambition and our role as a ‘living lab’ to explore new mobility solutions that can make the guest experience even more seamless and convenient,” said Thien Kwee Eng, CEO of SDC.

Guests could book AVs through TADA’s booking platform. The application will use GPS data to suggest the nearest available PUDO points across the island.

TADA said they will work with the Land Transport Authority to ensure AVs follow safety and operational protocols. Ahead of the pilot, SDC and TADA will also conduct further trials to validate routes, booking, boarding and safety procedures.

The service will be complimentary for guests during the pilot period and will operate from 1 p.m. to 7 p.m. Guests can scan a QR code on the on-site wayfinding signage for more information.

Subsequent phases of the service will extend its network across Sentosa, subject to LTA’s regulatory approvals.

data.title: Private hire car buyers face tighter loan limits
data.description:
Commercial vehicles and motorcycles stay exempt as do vehicles owned by businesses.

Individuals buying private hire cars (PHCs) will be subject to the same motor vehicle financing restrictions as private car buyers from 30 October.

The changes were announced by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, the Ministry of Transport, the Ministry of Trade and Industry, and the Ministry of Law.

Individual buyers of vehicles with an open market value (OMV) of $20,000 or less can borrow up to 70% of the purchase price, including applicable taxes and the Certificate of Entitlement (COE), where applicable.

For vehicles with an OMV of more than $20,000, the maximum loan-to-value (LTV) ratio will be capped at 60%.

All motor vehicle financing arrangements will also be subject to a maximum tenure of seven years.

The restrictions will apply to individuals obtaining vehicle loans from financial institutions and licensed or exempt moneylenders, as well as those entering into hire purchase or conditional sale agreements.

They will cover individual-owned PHCs with sales agreements signed on or after 30 October. Where no sales agreement is signed, the rules will apply to vehicles with COEs obtained on or after that date.

Commercial vehicles, business-owned PHCs and motorcycles will remain exempt.

The groups said the changes aim to prevent individuals from using the PHC classification to circumvent financing restrictions imposed on private car buyers.

data.title: Singapore-Philippines power deals explore cross-border links
data.description:
Agreements also cover advanced nuclear technology and workforce development.

Singapore and the Philippines have agreed to explore cross-border electricity interconnections and deepen cooperation on nuclear energy, as both countries seek to expand regional energy cooperation and diversify their energy options.

Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry Tan See Leng and Philippine Energy Secretary Sharon Garin exchanged Letters of Intent (LOIs) during the opening day of the Singapore International Energy Week (SIEW) Summit 2026.

The interconnection LOI seeks to explore opportunities for cross-border electricity connectivity, which could enable participating countries to trade electricity and make better use of complementary energy resources.

Both sides may engage companies with credible proposals to assess the technical, economic, financial, and commercial aspects of potential interconnections alongside coordination on relevant regulatory approvals and licences.

The LOI also aims to advance the ASEAN Power Grid vision by accelerating efforts to finalise the ASEAN Submarine Power Cable Development Framework.

Under the nuclear LOI, both economies aim to deepen cooperation in advanced nuclear technology, human resource development, the nuclear fuel cycle, nuclear waste management, and civil liability frameworks.

Cooperation includes the exchange of information and expertise amongst government officials and relevant experts, as well as research collaboration.

Both sides also affirmed that nuclear energy cooperation should be pursued safely, securely, and sustainably, consistent with nuclear non-proliferation principles, and applicable international safeguards.

At the SIEW Ministerial Dialogue on regional energy cooperation, Garin emphasised the need for compatible regulations, complementary energy resources, and mutually beneficial arrangements to advance cross-border electricity interconnections.

The Philippines is also exploring electricity links with Malaysia and Indonesia, with bilateral agreements and government coordination seen as key to advancing regional projects.
